title: Microsoft Targets Rogue AI Agents With Dynamic Permissions, Risk Scoring
description: Microsoft announced new security controls to monitor and restrict AI agents operating within enterprise environments, treating them as insiders rather than trusted software. These controls include Dynamic Permissions that grant minimal access initially and adjust permissions per task, Dynamic Agent Risk scoring that continuously evaluates agent risk based on multiple signals, and Dynamic Conditional Access that scales permissions or requires human approval based on risk. The system also includes Playbooks and Guardian Agents to enforce security responses. This approach aims to mitigate risks from AI agents that may be overprivileged, make mistakes, be manipulated, or be compromised.
aiSummary: Microsoft is enhancing its Project Perception security system to address risks posed by AI agents deployed internally in organizations. Recognizing that AI agents can act with significant privileges and impact critical processes, Microsoft treats them as insiders capable of mistakes or compromise. The new features include Dynamic Permissions, which start agents with minimal access and grant permissions per task with expiration or reduction as tasks change. Dynamic Agent Risk assigns continuously updated risk scores based on agent activity and environmental signals, influencing access controls via Dynamic Conditional Access. This access can be scaled back, limited to read-only, or halted if risk is high. Playbooks define security responses, and Guardian Agents execute containment actions. The system supports discovery of 60 agent types, including popular AI coding assistants.
aiImpact: The controls aim to reduce the risk of unauthorized or harmful actions by AI agents within enterprise systems by limiting their access dynamically and requiring human oversight for high-impact actions. This reduces the potential damage from compromised or malfunctioning AI agents. There is no indication of active exploitation or inherent vulnerability; rather, this is a proactive security enhancement to manage AI agent risks.
